title: How much does broker execution actually affect your automated strategy's live results?
author: socialwhizca
selftext:
Been running a couple of automated strategies (MT5 EAs, nothing fancy) and the backtests look great, but I keep reading that live gets wrecked by execution, slippage, requotes, spread widening, stuff a backtest never captures.

Trying to work out how much of that is the broker vs just the reality of live markets. For those running bots live: did switching brokers actually move the needle on your live-vs-backtest gap, or is a chunk of slippage unavoidable no matter where you are?

I'm on AvaTrade (MT5, they allow EAs, and the fixed spreads at least make cost modelling cleaner) and it's held up ok so far, but curious what execution setups the algo people here have landed on and why.
